question: Two careful engineers implementing this rule independently, with only this contract, would produce DIFFERENT behavior on some input (the rule is ambiguous, under-specified, or relies on unstated host facts).

rules.text: The result is compact JSON: no whitespace anywhere outside text values. A map is an opening brace, its entries as key-text, a colon and the rendered value, separated by commas, and a closing brace; an empty map is the two braces alone. A list is its elements rendered in their own order between square brackets, separated by commas. true, false and none render as "true", "false" and "null".

KEY ORDER, applied to the entries of EVERY map, the table itself and every map nested at any depth (directly or inside a list): ascending order of each key's sequence of 16-bit code units, compared unit by unit, a proper prefix first. A character beyond the basic multilingual plane counts as its surrogate pair, so it sorts before the private-use and compatibility characters at the top of the basic plane. No key is special: digit-only keys sort as text ("10" precedes "9"). The order the entries arrive in never matters.
A list keeps its elements in their own order; only map entries are reordered.

A text, key or value, renders between double quotes with exactly these escapes: quotation mark and backslash are preceded by a backslash; backspace, form feed, line feed, carriage return and tab become backslash-b, -f, -n, -r, -t; every other control character (code 0 through 31) becomes backslash-u and four LOWERCASE hex digits. Everything else is written raw: solidus, delete, the line and paragraph separators, and every non-ASCII character. Keys sort (R2) on their raw text, never on the escaped form.

Positive zero renders "0". Any other finite number renders by the ECMAScript Number-to-String algorithm. Take the shortest decimal digit string d (k digits, no leading or trailing zero) and the integer n such that the magnitude is d times ten to the power n - k and that round-trips to the same double (the closest to the exact value when several are shortest). Then: when k <= n <= 21, write d followed by n - k zeros; when 0 < n <= 21, write the first n digits, a point, and the rest; when -6 < n <= 0, write "0.", then -n zeros, then d; otherwise write the first digit, a point and the remaining digits when k > 1, then "e", the sign of n - 1 ("+" or "-") and its magnitude. A negative number carries a leading "-". So 255 is "255", 1e20 is "100000000000000000000", 1e21 is "1e+21", 0.000001 is "0.000001" and 1e-7 is "1e-7".

A number that is NaN, +Infinity, -Infinity or negative zero, anywhere in the table, makes the whole call throw; nothing is rendered CITED FIDELITY package — JSON has no form that tells these apart from zero or none
